chapters.title: Steel, Quietly
chapters.intro: Sport watches without the noise. Original dials, honest cases, and bracelets that still close the way they did on the first day.

chapters.title: Dress Hours
chapters.intro: Watches from the decades when a watch was made to be worn under a cuff and noticed only by the person wearing it.

chapters.title: Light, Held
chapters.intro: Diamonds and platinum from the Jazz Age, when New York and Paris jewelers built pieces that moved like light.

chapters.title: Colour, Considered
chapters.intro: Sapphire, emerald, and ruby at their most celebrated. Shown here as references for the calibre of colour we look for.

pieces.title: Submariner Date
pieces.headline: The first Submariner Date with a sapphire crystal, on its early matte dial.
story: The 16800 arrived around 1979 and quietly modernised the Submariner: a sapphire crystal in place of acrylic, a quickset date, and water resistance raised to 300 metres. Early examples kept the matte black dial and painted tritium markers of the reference before it.
This example shows exactly that transitional dial, marked 1000ft = 300m with the "T < 25" tritium signature at six o'clock. The markers have aged to a warm cream that matches the hands.
provenance: Matte dial with tritium lume, correct for early production
Photographed on its cushion, front, back, and profile
pieces.condition: Honest wear consistent with age. Light marks to the bezel insert and bracelet. Lume aged evenly.

pieces.title: GMT-Master II
pieces.headline: Three time zones, read at a glance, on a black bezel.
story: The 16710 was made from 1989 to 2007 and is the GMT-Master II many collectors consider the purest: a 40 mm steel Oyster case, an independently set hour hand, and a 24-hour bezel that lets one watch keep three time zones.
This one wears the all-black bezel insert, the most discreet of the three the reference was offered with, and the red-tipped 24-hour hand that has marked the GMT since 1955.
provenance: Shown with its green Rolex box
Photographed front-on and on the box
pieces.condition: Very good. Crisp dial and hands. Light bracelet wear.
specs: Hours, minutes, seconds, date, second time zone

pieces.title: Speedmaster Professional
pieces.headline: The chronograph NASA qualified in 1965, still made to the same idea.
story: NASA tested chronographs to destruction in 1964 and 1965 and the Speedmaster was the one that survived. Buzz Aldrin wore his on the lunar surface in July 1969, which is why the Professional is still called the Moonwatch.
It remains a manual-wind chronograph under a hesalite crystal, with a black dial, three registers, and a tachymeter bezel. It asks you to wind it each morning, and that ritual is much of the charm.
provenance: Detail views show the profile and the engraved caseback of the same reference
pieces.condition: Very good. Original bracelet with folding clasp.

pieces.title: Royal Oak "Jumbo" Extra-Thin
pieces.headline: Gérald Genta's octagon, at the original 39 mm and 8.1 mm thin.
story: When Audemars Piguet showed the Royal Oak in 1972, a steel watch priced like gold was a provocation. The 15202 kept the proportions of that first ref. 5402: 39 mm across, extra-thin, with the octagonal bezel held by eight hexagonal screws.
Inside is calibre 2121, the ultra-thin automatic shared with the original. The blue Petite Tapisserie dial is the colour most people picture when they hear the name.
provenance: Shown on the wrist for scale
pieces.condition: Very good. Brushed and polished surfaces crisp.

pieces.title: Nautilus
pieces.headline: The blue gradient dial, horizontally embossed, in a 40 mm steel case.
story: Gérald Genta drew the Nautilus in 1976 after the porthole of an ocean liner. The 5711/1A replaced the 3800 in 2006 and became the most sought-after steel watch of its time before Patek Philippe retired it in 2021.
The blue dial fades from light to near-black at the edge, under horizontal embossing. The integrated bracelet is finished by hand, alternately brushed and polished.
provenance: Official Patek Philippe photography

pieces.title: Calatrava
pieces.headline: The 1932 Calatrava that defined the round dress watch.
story: Reference 96 was introduced in 1932, the year the Stern family took over Patek Philippe, and it became the template for every round dress watch since: a plain 31 mm case, a sector of nothing but proportion, and small seconds above six.
This late-1930s example has a silvered dial with applied batons and a sunken small-seconds register. It sits on a dark leather strap, as it would have when new.
provenance: Late 1930s production, per the photographer's record
pieces.condition: Good for age. Dial with even, soft patina.

photos.alt: Patek Philippe Calatrava ref. 96 from the late 1930s with a silvered dial and small seconds, on a dark leather strap

pieces.title: Reverso Tribute Monoface
pieces.headline: A case that turns over, designed in 1931 for polo players.
story: The Reverso was made in 1931 so that officers playing polo in British India could flip the dial against the case and protect the crystal. The Tribute collection returns to the proportions and gadroons of those first cases.
This Monoface has a blue sunray dial with small seconds at six, on a strap made with Casa Fagliano, the Argentine polo-boot maker.
provenance: Shown in its presentation box
Casa Fagliano strap

pieces.title: Must de Cartier Tank
pieces.headline: Louis Cartier's 1917 rectangle, in gilded silver.
story: Louis Cartier drew the Tank in 1917, taking its lines from the tracks of the tanks on the Western Front. In 1977 Les Must de Cartier brought it to a new generation in vermeil, sterling silver with a heavy gold plating.
The cream dial carries black Roman numerals, a railway minute track, and blued-steel sword hands. The crown is set with a blue cabochon, as Cartier crowns have been for a century.
provenance: Les Must de Cartier line

photos.alt: Must de Cartier Tank in vermeil with a cream Roman numeral dial and black leather strap, on a dark blue background

pieces.title: Cosmograph Daytona
pieces.headline: The Zenith-powered Daytona, in 18 karat yellow gold.
story: From 1988 to 2000 the automatic Daytona ran on calibre 4030, Rolex's heavily reworked version of the Zenith El Primero. Collectors call these the Zenith Daytonas, and the yellow gold 16528 is the most luminous of them.
This example carries an S-prefix serial, which places it in the early 1990s. The white dial with black registers reads cleanly against the gold.
provenance: S-series serial, early 1990s
pieces.condition: Very good. Bracelet with light stretch for age.
specs: Automatic chronograph, Rolex calibre 4030 (Zenith El Primero base)

photos.alt: Rolex Cosmograph Daytona 16528 in yellow gold with a white dial and black chronograph registers

pieces.title: Asymmetrical Bracelet
pieces.headline: Made on the streets around ours, by the brothers who taught New York to set platinum.
story: Oscar and Nathan Heyman apprenticed with an uncle in Kharkov who supplied Fabergé. In New York Oscar first worked for Pierre Cartier, and in 1912 the brothers founded Oscar Heyman & Brothers, making pieces for Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels, and Shreve, Crump & Low before selling under their own name.
This diamond bracelet was shown in the Jazz Age exhibition at the Cleveland Museum of Art. Its panels break symmetry on purpose, which was a radical thing for a bracelet in the 1920s.
provenance: Exhibited: "Jazz Age: American Style in the 1920s", Cleveland Museum of Art
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale

photos.alt: Oscar Heyman and Brothers Art Deco diamond bracelet with asymmetrical geometric panels, displayed vertically on black

pieces.title: Brooch with Pendant
pieces.headline: A geometric diamond brooch with a single pearl drop.
story: Cartier's Art Deco brooches traded the garlands of the Belle Époque for open geometry: frames, steps, and triangles of diamonds set in platinum-white mounts.
This brooch suspends a pearl from a diamond triangle beneath an open rectangular frame. It was shown in the Jazz Age exhibition at the Cleveland Museum of Art.
provenance: Exhibited: "Jazz Age: American Style in the 1920s", Cleveland Museum of Art
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale

photos.alt: Cartier Art Deco diamond brooch with an open geometric frame and a pearl drop pendant, on dark fabric

pieces.title: Pendant Watch
pieces.headline: A chatelaine of platinum, diamonds, and pearls, with a watch hidden in the drop.
story: Van Cleef & Arpels won the grand prize at the 1925 Paris exposition that gave Art Deco its name. Two years later the house made this pendant in platinum, diamonds, and pearls, after the form of a chatelaine, the chains once worn at the belt to carry keys.
The slender watch sits inside the pendant at the bottom, its movement by an unrecorded craftsman. It is jewellery first, and a watch only for the person who knows to look.
provenance: Exhibited: "Jazz Age: American Style in the 1920s", Cleveland Museum of Art
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale

photos.alt: Van Cleef and Arpels 1927 pendant watch in platinum with diamonds and pearls, shaped like a chatelaine, on black

pieces.title: Iris Corsage Ornament
pieces.headline: Montana sapphires in a life-size iris, shown at the 1900 Paris Exposition.
story: At the turn of the century Tiffany & Co. made a series of realistic floral jewels, and this iris, designed by G. Paulding Farnham, was part of the firm's display at the Exposition Universelle of 1900 in Paris.

The petals are set with faceted blue sapphires from Montana that vary in tone and size, in oxidised silver. Citrines in gold collets suggest the bearding of the falls, and demantoid garnets set à jour form the leaves on an etched gold stem. It is in the collection of the Walters Art Museum, Baltimore.
provenance: Walters Art Museum, Baltimore (57.939)
Exposition Universelle, Paris, 1900
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale

pieces.title: Maximilian Emerald Ring
pieces.headline: The 21-carat Colombian emerald once worn by Mexico's emperor.
story: The emerald was once set in a ring worn by Ferdinand Maximilian Joseph, the Austrian archduke crowned Emperor of Mexico in 1864 and executed three years later.
Today it is mounted in a ring by Cartier, flanked by step-cut diamonds, and it is in the National Gem Collection at the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History in Washington.
provenance: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History, Washington
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale

pieces.title: Tutti Frutti Bracelet
pieces.headline: Carved emeralds, rubies, and sapphires, set the way Cartier learned from India.
story: In the 1920s Cartier began setting carved Indian emeralds, rubies, and sapphires among diamonds in platinum. The style was later nicknamed Tutti Frutti, and these bracelets became some of the most recognisable jewels of the Art Deco period.
This bracelet was shown in the Jazz Age exhibition at the Cleveland Museum of Art. Every leaf and berry is carved, so the surface reads like a garden rather than a row of stones.
provenance: Exhibited: "Jazz Age: American Style in the 1920s", Cleveland Museum of Art
Shown as a reference piece, not offered for sale
